lessons.title: Clothes
lessons.goal: Name clothes and say what you're looking for.

tip.title: Same clothes, different words
tip.body: Some clothes have different names in Spain and Latin America: a T-shirt is una camiseta in Spain but una playera in Mexico; a jacket is una chaqueta in Spain and una chamarra in Mexico; a jumper is un jersey in Spain and un suéter in most of Latin America. Pantalones (trousers) is usually plural: unos pantalones. In a shop, say Busco … (I'm looking for …).

phrases.note: Latin America also: Solo estoy viendo.

dialogue.title: In a clothes shop in Madrid

lines.name: Dependienta
lines.t: Hola, buenas. ¿Le puedo ayudar?
lines.n: Hello there. Can I help you?

lines.t: Hola. Busco una chaqueta.
lines.n: Hello. I'm looking for a jacket.

lines.name: Dependienta
lines.t: Las chaquetas están allí, al fondo.
lines.n: The jackets are over there, at the back.

lines.t: Gracias. Y también busco unos zapatos.
lines.n: Thanks. And I'm also looking for some shoes.

lines.name: Dependienta
lines.t: Los zapatos están en la planta de abajo.
lines.n: The shoes are on the floor below.

prompts.n: Tell the shop assistant you're looking for a T-shirt.
Say you're looking for a dress.

lessons.title: Colours & sizes
lessons.goal: Ask for a colour and a size and try things on.

tip.title: Colours come after the noun
tip.body: Colours follow the noun and agree with it: una falda roja, unos zapatos negros. Colours ending in -e or a consonant only change for plural: una camisa verde, dos camisas verdes; un jersey azul, dos jerseys azules. For clothing size, ask ¿Qué talla tiene? (In Mexico you'll also hear ¿Qué talla usa?). For shoes, Spain uses número: ¿Qué número tiene?

phrases.n: Do you have it in blue? (a feminine item, e.g. la camiseta)
phrases.note: For a masculine item: ¿Lo tiene en azul?
For a feminine item: ¿Me la puedo probar?
Too small: me queda pequeño/pequeña (Spain), me queda chico/chica (Mexico).

lines.t: Disculpe, ¿tiene esta camisa en azul?
lines.n: Excuse me, do you have this shirt in blue?

lines.name: Vendedor
lines.t: Sí, claro. ¿Qué talla usa?
lines.n: Yes, of course. What size are you?

lines.t: La mediana, por favor. ¿Me la puedo probar?
lines.n: The medium, please. Can I try it on?

lines.name: Vendedor
lines.t: Sí, los probadores están ahí.
lines.n: Yes, the fitting rooms are over there.

lines.t: Me queda un poco grande. ¿Tiene la chica?
lines.n: It's a bit big for me. Do you have the small?

prompts.n: Ask if they have it in black (a feminine item).
Ask if you can try it on (a masculine item).
Say it's too big for you.

tip.title: cuesta or cuestan?
tip.body: Use ¿Cuánto cuesta? for one thing and ¿Cuánto cuestan? for more than one: ¿Cuánto cuestan los zapatos? Spain pays in euros (veinte euros, cincuenta céntimos) and Mexico in pesos (doscientos pesos). In Mexico prices are written with the $ sign, which here means pesos. ¿Cuánto es? asks for the total.

lines.t: ¿Cuánto cuesta este jersey?
lines.n: How much is this jumper?

lines.name: Dependiente
lines.t: Cuesta treinta y cinco euros.
lines.n: It costs thirty-five euros.

lines.t: Vale, me lo llevo. ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?
lines.n: OK, I'll take it. Can I pay by card?

lines.name: Dependiente
lines.t: Sí, claro. Aquí tiene su ticket.
lines.n: Yes, of course. Here's your receipt.

prompts.n: Ask how much the dress costs.
Ask how much the trousers are.
Ask if you can pay by card.

lessons.title: este, ese: this and that
lessons.goal: Point to things with este/esta/estos/estas and ese/esa.

tip.title: Demonstratives match the noun
tip.body: "This" (near me) is este (masculine), esta (feminine), estos, estas (plural). "That" (near you, or a bit further) is ese, esa, esos, esas. They agree with the noun, just like colours: este jersey rojo, esta falda roja, estos zapatos rojos, esas camisas rojas. Without a noun they mean "this one / that one": Quiero este. (There is a third set, aquel/aquella, for things far away.)

prompts.n: Say this T-shirt is very cheap.
Ask how much those shoes are.

lessons.title: At the tianguis
lessons.goal: Follow prices and colours at a market.

phrases.note: A common market question for produce.

phrases.t: Le dejo las dos en trescientos cincuenta.
phrases.n: I'll let you have both for three hundred and fifty.

story.title: Sunday market in Oaxaca
story.intro: Ana is shopping at a street market in Oaxaca, Mexico, and stops at a stall selling handmade bags.

lines.name: Ana
lines.t: Buenos días. ¿Cuánto cuesta esta bolsa roja?
lines.n: Good morning. How much is this red bag?

lines.name: Vendedor
lines.t: Esa cuesta ciento ochenta pesos, señorita. Está hecha a mano.
lines.n: That one costs a hundred and eighty pesos, miss. It's handmade.

lines.name: Ana
lines.t: ¿Y esta verde?
lines.n: And this green one?

lines.name: Vendedor
lines.t: La verde es más grande, doscientos pesos.
lines.n: The green one is bigger, two hundred pesos.

lines.name: Ana
lines.t: Me gustan las dos. ¿Me hace un descuento?
lines.n: I like both. Can you give me a discount?

lines.name: Vendedor
lines.t: Ándele, le dejo las dos en trescientos cincuenta.
lines.n: Go on, I'll let you have both for three hundred and fifty.

lines.name: Ana
lines.t: ¡Perfecto! Me las llevo.
lines.n: Perfect! I'll take them.

questions.n: How much is the red bag?
How much does Ana pay for both?

branch.title: At a shop in Salamanca
branch.scene: You're in a clothes shop in Salamanca, Spain. You need a warm jacket for winter.
branch.name: Dependiente

hello.n: Good afternoon! Can I help you with anything?

choices.n: Yes, I'm looking for a jacket for the winter.

jacket.t: Mire, esta chaqueta negra es muy calentita. ¿Qué talla tiene?

choices.n: Medium. Can I try it on?

try.n: Of course, here you are. The fitting room is there. … How does it fit?

choices.n: It fits well. How much is it?
It's much too big for me.
Yes, perfect. How much is it?

choices.t: Vale, me la llevo. ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?
choices.n: OK, I'll take it. Can I pay by card?

choices.t: Es un poco cara… ¿Me la deja en treinta?
choices.n: It's a bit expensive… Will you let me have it for thirty?

haggle.t: Lo siento, aquí los precios son fijos.
haggle.n: Sorry, the prices here are fixed.

choices.t: Vale, no pasa nada. Me la llevo.

culture.title: Markets, euros and pesos
culture.body: Spain uses the euro, and Mexico the Mexican peso; in Mexico the $ sign on a price tag means pesos, not dollars. Most towns have a covered food market (mercado), and Mexico is famous for its tianguis, open-air street markets that set up on certain days of the week. In shops and supermarkets prices are fixed, and haggling would seem odd. At street markets and craft stalls, especially in Latin America, asking politely for a small discount (¿Me hace un descuento?) is sometimes accepted, but always keep it friendly.

phrases.n: Can you give me a discount?
phrases.note: Only at markets and stalls, not in shops.

free.n: You're out shopping. Say what you're looking for, its colour and size, and ask the price.
free.hint: Busco … · Quiero esta camiseta azul … · Talla mediana · ¿Cuánto cuesta? · Me lo llevo.
free.model: Hola, buenas tardes. Busco una camiseta. Me gusta mucho esta camiseta azul. ¿La tiene en talla mediana? ¿Cuánto cuesta? Veinte euros, perfecto, me la llevo.

prompts.n: At a market stall, ask politely for a discount.
Say you need some new shoes.
